headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage when ctx observes Claude Code outputs and Notion AI shares workspace content across sessions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx explicitly observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events, so it can ingest another agent’s outputs by default. Notion AI is RAG-style over workspace content and can surface attacker-controlled text from pages. That creates a direct instruction-hijack path between the pair, with no provenance guard documented.
conditions: IF ctx parses Claude Code event payloads as instructions or context, injection is reachable.
IF Notion workspace content contains adversarial prompts, ctx may consume them indirectly.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of Claude Code event text by ctx.
Add provenance tags to all Notion-sourced snippets before reuse.
Restrict ctx to allowlisted event fields only.
Review one sample PostToolUse payload for instruction-like text.
requires-engineering: insert a sanitization layer between Notion content and ctx.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, MCP servers, harness records, graph data, and runtime logs, while Notion AI reads workspace pages and databases under the user’s OAuth scope. Because Notion AI is vendor-hosted and ctx can observe tool events, sensitive workspace material can flow into a third-party backend and then into ctx-visible logs or outputs.
conditions: IF the workspace contains secrets, PHI, or regulated data, leakage impact increases.
IF ctx logs or re-emits Notion-derived content, the data leaves the original workspace boundary.
mitigations: Remove sensitive pages from the shared workspace before use.
Limit Notion AI access to a non-sensitive subspace.
Turn off or redact ctx runtime logs for Notion-derived content.
Audit one recent Notion AI answer for sensitive-source leakage.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on both sides.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and filesystem access, while Notion AI also supports multiple instances with shared workspace state across members. The pair can therefore contend over shared mutable knowledge artifacts even though Notion AI cannot write the host filesystem. The conflict is real but narrower than unrestricted same-dir writes.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same Notion page or linked workspace artifact, last-write conflicts can occur.
IF ctx mirrors workspace state into files, stale overwrites become possible.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole editor for each page.
Use page-level locks or naming conventions for ownership.
Refresh ctx state before any writeback.
Compare timestamps before accepting edits.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks across the pair.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is designed to observe Claude Code events, so its outputs can become inputs to downstream reasoning. Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, which can treat prior summaries as authoritative unless explicitly challenged. That creates a plausible error-amplification loop, though Notion’s limited action scope keeps it below high.
conditions: IF ctx writes a summary into Notion and Notion AI later answers from that summary, errors can cascade.
IF either agent is used as the sole source of truth, verification is bypassed.
mitigations: Require a human check before publishing summaries.
Mark ctx-generated notes as untrusted.
Ask Notion AI to cite source pages for each claim.
Cross-check one critical answer against the original page.
requires-engineering: add verification prompts or citation enforcement.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion vendor backends and downstream model providers, while ctx also calls external APIs such as GitHub and Claude Code. The profiles do not prove a specific residency mismatch, but they do show mixed third-party processing of workspace data, which is enough to raise a compliance concern under uncertainty.
conditions: IF regulated or region-bound data is stored in Notion pages, third-party processing may violate policy.
IF the workspace contains data subject to retention or export rules, vendor processing must be reviewed.
mitigations: Inventory regulated data in the workspace.
Restrict Notion AI to non-regulated pages.
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings.
Export one sample page to confirm data handling.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
